title: Guitar and banjo in larger bands, and pianists Frank Cuny and Tom Zimmerman
summary: DeDroit says he preferred bass, then describes pianists Frank Cuny and the theater organist Zimmerman.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: No, no, no, no. I used to get the guitar. As the, well, according to some of the other interviews I've read, originally like some of the Dixieland bands here used the guitar a lot and then they found the- They used the banjo and then they switched the guitar. And then the banjo came in and then they went back to the guitar as time went on. What time did you incorporate a banjo or I mean a guitar, banjo then guitar in your larger orchestra? I used the guitar.

I used the guitar at the Beverly Gardens and I used them on Biloxi because he didn't play banjo. Uh-huh. But he played so much guitar. You know what I mean? They played. They loved it and they played. That's all. But the original was just five men without any bass. And I always thought that I should have always had a bass instead of the banjo. Because the bass is really- but fortunately I had a piano players who liked the play and knew that the bass had come out, you know? And Frank Cuny, I can tell you, he had a callous on. He was an all-round pianist. I wouldn't call him a hot man but he had a wonderful memory and very intelligent and had a firm and precise. But Zillerman was a great pianist. Zillerman, I told you, he was a fagin. And he was an organist in a trilling in the theater. He always worked in the picture theaters, you know? And he played the organ. And he never did have any music, he'd make it up and he went along. And I went in there one day and he was playing the Grand March. I said, Tom, what's the title of the Grand March? It's beautiful. He said, title? He said, I made it up. Well I said, how do you do it? He said, well I think about Aida and I play something like it. That's all. But he plays his own numbers. He steals the format but he doesn't play the music. See what I mean? Like we take like the Grand March from Aida. You know he knows. She's the king and queen. He plays something like that. I never heard a man play something. But that kind of music should have been recorded. It was beautiful.
